If an error occurs after streaming has started, the server emits a line with an `error` property in the NDJSON stream and the HTTP status stays 200. Docs example: {"error":"an error was encountered while running the model"}.

Robust client rule: parse each line separately, check for an `error` key before reading content, and treat a stream that ends without done:true as incomplete. A reader that only joins `response` fields can return partial text and silently drop the error line.
Clients that expect a single JSON object from a streaming-default endpoint fail with parse errors (e.g. 'JSON Parse error: Unexpected EOF'); the workaround is stream:false.

If an error occurs mid-stream, the error will be returned as an object in the `application/x-ndjson` format with an `error` property. Since the response has already started, the status code of the response will not be changed.

Ollama documents that errors during streaming arrive as NDJSON objects with an error property. Once streaming starts, the response status is not changed. That means an application which checks only HTTP 200 can miss a later failure. Official error reference

Ollama streams several API responses as newline-delimited JSON so callers can display tokens as they arrive. Streaming lowers perceived latency for long generations, but the client must parse multiple JSON objects instead of one response body.

/api/generate and /api/chat stream by default; the stream is NDJSON served as application/x-ndjson, one JSON object per line. Setting "stream": false returns a single application/json object with the full text and done:true.

Final-chunk usage fields: total_duration, load_duration, prompt_eval_count, prompt_eval_cached_count, prompt_eval_duration, eval_count, eval_duration. All durations are nanoseconds; counts are tokens. Usage appears only in the done:true chunk.
Output tokens per second = eval_count / eval_duration * 10^9 (eval_duration is nanoseconds). The docs example 18 tokens in 52,479,709 ns is about 343 tokens/s.

Ollama runs as a native Windows application, including NVIDIA and AMD Radeon GPU support. After installing Ollama for Windows, Ollama will run in the background and the `ollama` command line is available in `cmd`, `powershell` or your favorite terminal application. As usual the Ollama [API](/api) will be served on `http://localhost:11434`.
